chains.title: ATF3-mediated effect at the enhancer-like element

links.claim: ATF3's own QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger in-vitro binding to alt C, but this does not establish occupancy in adipose precursors. The variant-overlapping ChIP peak is from HCT116, and no matching preadipocyte peak is reported; absence may also reflect lack of an assay. ATF3 is a candidate, not a demonstrated mediator. Its bZIP-related candidate JUN also has an alt-favoring model, so the evidence does not distinguish them; ATF3 has the larger predicted binding effect, while JUN is more highly expressed in the proxy.

The variant lies in the enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3181208. The nearby SCREEN record is EH38E3181207, and the reported activity maxima are not biosample-specific, so they do not establish activity of the variant-containing cCRE in adipose precursors.
FTO is prioritized for associated traits by L2G, but the supplied evidence does not connect EH38E3181208 directly to FTO. The reported FTO eQTL is in skeletal muscle, not adipose.
Subcutaneous adipose is a plausible context because ATF3 is expressed there, but it is only a proxy for preadipocytes and no relevant-context ATF3 occupancy is shown.

The variant is strongly associated with obesity, with ref T reported as the effect/risk allele. This does not establish that an ATF3-to-FTO effect mediates the association or whether greater ATF3 binding increases or decreases regulatory activity.

predictions: In relevant adipose precursor cells, ATF3 should occupy the variant-containing element and show greater occupancy or binding on C than T; ATF3 perturbation should alter the element's activity in an allele-dependent manner.
Compared with the null chain, this model predicts an ATF3-dependent effect of T versus C. It does not specify the direction of FTO expression change.
falsified_if: Relevant-cell assays show no ATF3 occupancy or no ATF3-dependent difference between T and C in element activity.

The aim of this study is to develop, validate, and apply a cost-effective 4-plex high-resolution melting (HRM) assay for simultaneous detection of FTO (rs9939609 and rs1421085) and PPAR-γ (rs1801282 and rs3856806) variants using standard laboratory equipment.
In the obesity group, the rs1421085 exhibited the strongest effect, with an odds ratio (OR) of 2.16 (95% CI: 1.58–2.95).

This meta-analysis provides strong evidence that FTO polymorphisms, particularly rs1421085 and rs9939609, are significantly associated with increased susceptibility to obesity in adults, while their impact on overweight is comparatively weaker.

Based on findings that experimental manipulation of the RNA m6A methylation in animal experiments can affect anxiety, and given that the C-allele of FTO rs1421085 had a significant association with indicators of overweight and obesity in our previous study, we have examined the possible association of FTO rs1421085 genotype with neuroticism in the same longitudinally observed sample.

Conclusively, an overweight and obesity-related variant of FTO, the gene encoding an RNA m6A demethylase, was associated with lower neuroticism, this association being subject to gender and cohort effects.

FTO variants showed mixed results, with rs9939609 (OR = 3.72, P = 0.009) and rs1421085 (OR = 3.22, P < 0.001) variants being associated with obesity and higher body mass index (BMI) in Indonesians, but no significant findings in Malaysians.
